a 120 kDa protein, cranin, is involved in the binding of laminin by cell surfaces, and is also involved in the attachment of cells to laminin substrata.
the laminin-binding 120 kDa protein cranin is a major HNK-1-positive protein of the neural cell membrane and that it is involved in axonal guidance.

the role of the extracellular matrix (ECM) in the developing and mature nervous system, and with the identification of the molecules that are responsible for the effects of the ECM.
the characterization of a novel class of membrane proteins that may be important for the regulation of axonal growth and guidance.
the identification of a new class of proteins associated with axonal outgrowth, which may be important in the guidance of neuritic outgrowth and neuronal cell migration during development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cranin family of proteins are important for the attachment and/or migration of neural cells in response to laminin.
the 3070/4/199 antigens represent a novel set of proteins associated with the axonal growth of neurons, and that they are likely to be important in the development of the nervous system.
the cranin antigen is a 120 kDa glycoprotein that is present on the surface of a wide variety of cells and is a major laminin-binding protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cranin antigens are important for the binding of laminin by neurons and reactive glia, and that the binding of laminins by cranins is important for the guidance of axons, the attachment of neurons to laminin, and possibly the migration and differentiation of neurons.
laminin is a multifunctional protein that can bind to and interact with several different cell membrane components.
laminin, which is a component of the basement membrane, is a major component of a complex set of extracellular matrix molecules that are involved in the regulation of neural development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cranin is a laminin binding molecule that is important in the growth of neurons.
the 3070/4 antigens are a family of laminin-binding proteins that appear to be involved in the response of neurons and reactive astrocytes to laminin in vitro and in vivo.
the 125 and 170/ 180 kDa HNK-1+ antigens, together with laminin, are likely to play important roles in the regulation of neural development.
